questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together, how much time will they take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12. Time = 12 minutes.

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a cistern in 12 hours. Due to a leak in the bottom, it is filled in 15 hours. If the cistern is full, in how much time will the leak empty it?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/12 - 1/15 = (5 - 4)/60 = 1/60. Leak alone empties full cistern in 60 hours.

questions.questionText: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a tank in 6 hours. After working together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B can fill the remaining part in 7 hours. How many hours will C alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: In 2 hours, A+B+C fill 2/6 = 1/3 of the tank. Remaining = 2/3. A and B fill 2/3 in 7 hours => A+B fill the whole tank in 7 * (3/2) = 10.5 hours (rate = 2/21). Rate of C = 1/6 - 2/21 = (7 - 4)/42 = 3/42 = 1/14. C alone takes 14 hours.
questions.concept: Partial Fill and Isolated Pipe Duration

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 37.5 minutes and 45 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened. The cistern will be filled in just half an hour if pipe B is turned off after:
questions.explanation: Total capacity = LCM(75/2, 45) = 225 units. Rate of A = 6 units/min, Rate of B = 5 units/min. Pipe A works for the full 30 minutes: 30 * 6 = 180 units. Remaining work for B = 225 - 180 = 45 units. Time for B = 45 / 5 = 9 minutes.
questions.concept: Fixed Target Fill Time Pipe Shutdown

questions.questionText: A cistern has two taps which can fill it in 12 minutes and 15 minutes respectively. There is also a waste pipe. When all three are opened, the empty cistern is full in 20 minutes. How long will the waste pipe take to empty the full cistern?

Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 hours and 12 hours respectively and a third pipe can empty it in 4 hours. If the pipes are opened in order at 8 am, 9 am, and 11 am respectively, at what time will the tank be emptied?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A (inlet) = +4, B (inlet) = +5, C (outlet) = -15 units/hr. At 8 am A opens: by 11 am (3 hrs), A fills 3 * 4 = 12 units. At 9 am B opens: by 11 am (2 hrs), B fills 2 * 5 = 10 units. Total water at 11 am = 22 units. At 11 am, all three operate: net rate = 4 + 5 - 15 = -6 units/hr (emptying). Time to empty 22 units = 22 / 6 = 3 2/3 hours = 3 hrs 40 mins. Time = 11:00 am + 3 hrs 40 mins = 2:40 pm.

questions.questionText: A booster pump can be used for filling as well as for emptying a tank. The capacity of the tank is 2400 m^3. The emptying capacity of the pump is 10 m^3/min higher than its filling capacity. If the pump takes 8 minutes less to empty the tank than to fill it, what is the filling capacity of the pump?
Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 24 minutes and 32 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together, after how much time should B be closed so that the tank is full in 18 minutes?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 96 units. A = 4, B = 3. A runs for all 18 mins: 18 * 4 = 72 units. Remaining for B = 96 - 72 = 24 units. Time B is open = 24 / 3 = 8 minutes.

questions.questionText: A bath can be filled by the cold water pipe in 10 minutes and by the hot water pipe in 15 minutes. A person leaves the bathroom after turning on both pipes and returns at the moment when the bath should be full. Finding that the waste pipe had remained open, he closes it. In 4 minutes more, the bath is full. In what time would the waste pipe empty it?
questions.explanation: Expected fill time = (10 * 15) / 25 = 6 minutes. In 6 minutes, water filled = 6 * (1/6 - 1/W). Then in 4 mins of (A+B), extra water = 4 * (1/6) = 2/3. So water lost through waste pipe in 6 mins = 2/3 of tank. Rate of waste pipe = (2/3) / 6 = 1/9. Waste pipe empties in 9 minutes.

questions.questionText: One pipe can fill a tank 3 times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 36 minutes, how much time will the slower pipe alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Ratio of rates = 3 : 1. Combined rate = 4 units/min. Total capacity = 36 * 4 = 144 units. Slower pipe (rate 1) takes 144 / 1 = 144 minutes.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A = 4, B = 3. In 4 minutes: 4 * 7 = 28 units. Remaining = 32 units. Time for B = 32 / 3 = 10 2/3 mins = 10 mins 40 secs. Total time = 4 + 10 min 40 sec = 14 min 40 sec.

questions.questionText: A leak in the bottom of a tank can empty the full tank in 8 hours. An inlet pipe fills water at the rate of 6 litres a minute. When the tank is full, the inlet is opened and due to the leak, the tank is empty in 12 hours. How many litres does the cistern hold?
questions.explanation: Inlet rate = 1/8 - 1/12 = (3 - 2)/24 = 1/24 of tank per hour. Inlet fills 6 litres/min = 360 litres/hour. (1/24) of Tank = 360 litres => Capacity = 360 * 24 = 8,640 litres.

questions.questionText: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 5 hours and 6 hours respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, how much time will they take to fill the tank?
Three taps A, B, and C can fill a tank in 12, 15, and 20 hours respectively. If A is open all the time and B and C are open for one hour each alternately, the tank will be full in:
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A = 5, B = 4, C = 3. Hour 1 (A+B): 5 + 4 = 9 units. Hour 2 (A+C): 5 + 3 = 8 units. 2-hour cycle = 9 + 8 = 17 units. In 3 cycles (6 hours): 3 * 17 = 51 units. Remaining = 60 - 51 = 9 units. In hour 7, (A+B) fills exactly 9 units. Total time = 7 hours.

questions.questionText: A large tanker can be filled by two pipes A and B in 60 minutes and 40 minutes respectively. How many minutes will it take to fill the tanker from empty state if B is used for half the time and A and B together for the other half?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 120 units. A = 2 units/min, B = 3 units/min. Let total time be 2t. For time t, only B operates: 3t. For time t, A+B operate: 5t. Total = 3t + 5t = 8t = 120 => t = 15 mins. Total time = 2t = 30 minutes.

questions.questionText: A water tank has three taps: A, B, and C. Tap A, when opened alone, can fill the tank in 4 hours; tap B in 6 hours; and tap C can empty the full tank in 3 hours. If all taps are opened simultaneously at 1:00 PM, what fraction of the tank is filled by 3:00 PM?
questions.explanation: Net hourly rate = 1/4 + 1/6 - 1/3 = (3 + 2 - 4)/12 = 1/12 of tank per hour. In 2 hours (1 pm to 3 pm), fraction filled = 2 * (1/12) = 1/6.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12 minutes and 16 minutes respectively. Both are opened together for a certain time, but being clogged, only 7/8 of the full quantity of water flows through A and 5/6 through B. The obstructions, however, being suddenly removed, the cistern is filled in 3 minutes from that moment. How long was it before the obstructions were removed?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 48 units. Normal rates: A = 4, B = 3 (Total = 7 units/min). Clogged rates: A = 4 * 7/8 = 3.5, B = 3 * 5/6 = 2.5 (Total clogged = 6 units/min). In final 3 minutes (normal): 3 * 7 = 21 units. Remaining filled during clogged phase = 48 - 21 = 27 units. Clogged duration = 27 / 6 = 4.5 minutes.

questions.questionText: Two pipes can separately fill a tank in 20 hours and 30 hours respectively. Both the pipes are opened to fill the tank but when the tank is 1/3 full, a leak develops in the tank through which 1/3 of water supplied by both pipes goes out. What is the total time taken to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Normal combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 of tank per hour. Time for first 1/3 = (1/3) / (1/12) = 4 hours. For remaining 2/3, effective rate = 1/12 * (1 - 1/3) = (1/12) * (2/3) = 1/18 per hour. Time for remaining 2/3 = (2/3) / (1/18) = 12 hours. Total time = 4 + 12 = 16 hours.

questions.questionText: A tank can be filled by two pipes in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. When the tank was empty, the two pipes were opened. After some time, the first pipe was turned off and the tank was filled in 18 minutes in total. After how much time from the start was the first pipe turned off?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A = 3, B = 2. B works for 18 mins: 18 * 2 = 36 units. Remaining for A = 60 - 36 = 24 units. Time A was open = 24 / 3 = 8 minutes.

questions.questionText: Pipe A can fill a tank in 16 minutes and Pipe B can empty it in 24 minutes. If both pipes are opened alternately for 1 minute each starting with Pipe A, in how much time will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 48 units. A = +3 units, B = -2 units. In 2 minutes, net fill = +1 unit. Target before last filling step = 48 - 3 = 45 units. Time for 45 units = 45 * 2 = 90 minutes. In minute 91, Pipe A adds +3 units, reaching 45 + 3 = 48 units (full). Total time = 91 minutes.

questions.questionText: A cistern can be filled by two pipes in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. When the cistern is empty, both pipes are opened. After how many minutes should the second pipe be turned off so that the cistern may be completely full in 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A = 3, B = 2. A runs for 15 mins: 15 * 3 = 45 units. Remaining for B = 60 - 45 = 15 units. Time for B = 15 / 2 = 7.5 minutes.

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. Due to a leak in the bottom, it fills it in 20 hours. If the tank is full, how much time will the leak take to empty it?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/15 - 1/20 = (4 - 3)/60 = 1/60. Emptying time = 60 hours.

questions.questionText: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a cistern in 10, 12, and 15 hours respectively. If pipe A is opened all the time and B and C are opened for one hour each alternately, in how many hours will the cistern be full?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A = 6, B = 5, C = 4. Hour 1 (A+B): 11 units. Hour 2 (A+C): 10 units. 2-hour cycle = 21 units. In 2 cycles (4 hours): 42 units. Hour 5 (A+B): 42 + 11 = 53 units. Remaining = 7 units. (A+C) does this in 7/10 hours. Total = 5 7/10 hours; for exact: 5 2/3 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 36 minutes and 45 minutes respectively. A waste pipe C can carry off 30 litres per minute. If all the pipes are opened when the tank is full, it is emptied in 60 minutes. Find the capacity of the tank.
questions.explanation: The waste pipe removes the tank contents in 60 minutes, so its net emptying rate is 1/60 tank per minute. The two inlets together fill 1/36 + 1/45 = 9/180 = 1/20 tank per minute. Therefore, the waste pipe fills at 1/60 + 1/20 = 1/15 tank per minute. If this is 30 litres per minute, the tank capacity is 30*15 = 450 litres.

questions.questionText: A tank has two pipes. The first pipe can fill it in 45 minutes and the second can empty it in 1 hour. In what time will the empty tank be filled if both pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Fill rate = 1/45 - 1/60 = (4 - 3)/180 = 1/180 per minute = 180 minutes = 3 hours.

questions.questionText: Eight pipes are fitted to a water tank. Some of these are water pipes to fill the tank and the remaining are waste pipes used to empty the tank. Each water pipe can fill the tank in 12 hours and each waste pipe can empty it in 36 hours. On opening all the pipes, an empty tank is filled in 3 hours. Find the number of filling pipes.
questions.explanation: Let filling pipes be f, waste pipes be (8 - f). Rate = f/12 - (8 - f)/36 = 1/3 => 3f - (8 - f) = 12 => 4f - 8 = 12 => 4f = 20 => f = 5.

questions.questionText: Two taps A and B can fill a tank in 10 hours and 15 hours respectively. If both taps are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be full?
A cistern is normally filled in 8 hours but takes 2 hours longer to fill because of a leak in its bottom. If the cistern is full, the leak will empty it in:
questions.explanation: Normal time = 8 hrs. With leak = 10 hrs. Leak rate = 1/8 - 1/10 = (5 - 4)/40 = 1/40. Time to empty = 40 hours.

questions.questionText: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 18 minutes, while drain C can empty a full tank in 36 minutes. A and B run together for 3 minutes; then C is opened as well. How long from the start will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Use a 36-unit tank. A fills 3 units/min, B fills 2 units/min, and C empties 1 unit/min. During the first 3 minutes A and B fill 15 units, leaving 21. With all three open, the net rate is 3 + 2 - 1 = 4 units/min, so the remaining time is 21/4 = 5.25 minutes. Total time is 3 + 5.25 = 8.25 minutes, or 8 minutes 15 seconds.
questions.concept: Switching from Joint Inflow to Net Flow

questions.questionText: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a tank in 12, 15, and 20 minutes respectively. If all are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
A pipe can fill a tank in 3 hours. Due to a leak, it takes 3.5 hours to fill it. In how many hours can the leak alone empty a half-full tank?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/3 - 1/3.5 = 1/3 - 2/7 = (7 - 6)/21 = 1/21 per hour. Leak empties full tank in 21 hours. For half-full tank: 21 / 2 = 10.5 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours respectively. If they are opened on alternate hours starting with pipe A, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 36 units. A = 3, B = 2. In 2 hours: 5 units. In 7 cycles (14 hours): 7 * 5 = 35 units. Remaining = 1 unit. A fills 1 unit in 1/3 hour. Total time = 14 1/3 hours.

questions.questionText: A swimming pool is filled by three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously fill the pool in the same time during which the pool is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the pool 5 hours faster than the first pipe and 4 hours slower than the third pipe. Find the time required by the first pipe.
questions.explanation: Let time for 3rd pipe = t. Then 2nd pipe = t + 4, 1st pipe = t + 9. 1/(t + 9) + 1/(t + 4) = 1/t. Shortcut: t = √(9 * 4) = 6 hours. Time for 1st pipe = 6 + 9 = 15 hours.

questions.questionText: A tap can fill an empty tank in 12 hours and a leakage can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If both are opened together, the tank will be filled in:

Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 15 hours and 20 hours respectively, while a third pipe C can empty the full cistern in 25 hours. All the three pipes are opened in the beginning. After 10 hours, C is closed. In how much time will the cistern be full?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 300 units. A = 20, B = 15, C = -12. In 10 hours with all three: 10 * (20 + 15 - 12) = 10 * 23 = 230 units. Remaining = 300 - 230 = 70 units. With only A and B: rate = 35 units/hr. Time = 70 / 35 = 2 hours. Total time = 10 + 2 = 12 hours.

questions.questionText: A cistern can be filled by two pipes A and B in 4 hours and 6 hours respectively. If they are opened alternately for 1 hour each starting with pipe A, how many hours will it take to fill the cistern?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 12 units. A = 3, B = 2. 2-hour cycle = 5 units. In 2 cycles (4 hours): 10 units. Remaining = 2 units. A does 2 units in 2/3 hour. Total time = 4 2/3 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 14 hours and 16 hours respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage in the bottom it took 32 minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in what time will the leak empty it?
questions.explanation: Normal time = (14 * 16) / 30 = 224 / 30 = 7 hrs 28 mins. Time with leak = 7 hrs 28 mins + 32 mins = 8 hours. Leak rate = 30/224 - 1/8 = 30/224 - 28/224 = 2/224 = 1/112. Leak empties cistern in 112 hours.

questions.questionText: One pipe fills a water tank in 20 minutes and another fills it in 30 minutes. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill 50% of the tank?
questions.explanation: Full tank takes 12 minutes. 50% of the tank takes 12 / 2 = 6 minutes.

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a tank in 24 hours. If 3 more pipes of the same capacity are opened, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Total 4 identical pipes. Time = 24 / 4 = 6 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 minutes and 24 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together, after how much time should A be closed so that the tank is full in 16 minutes?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 72 units. A = 4, B = 3. B runs for 16 mins: 16 * 3 = 48 units. Remaining for A = 72 - 48 = 24 units. Time A was open = 24 / 4 = 6 minutes.

questions.questionText: If two pipes can fill a tank in 24 hours and 30 hours respectively, in how many hours will they together fill the tank?
A pipe of diameter d can drain a water pool in 40 minutes. How long will another pipe of diameter 2d take to drain the same pool?
questions.explanation: Flow rate is proportional to cross-sectional area (proportional to d^2). Doubling diameter increases flow rate by 2^2 = 4 times. Time = 40 / 4 = 10 minutes.

questions.questionText: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a tank in 6 hours, 9 hours, and 18 hours respectively. How long will they take to fill the tank if all are opened together?
A cistern can be filled by two pipes in 30 minutes and 40 minutes respectively. If both are opened together, when should the first pipe be turned off so that the cistern is full in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 120. A = 4, B = 3. B runs for 20 mins: 20 * 3 = 60 units. Remaining for A = 120 - 60 = 60 units. Time for A = 60 / 4 = 15 minutes.

questions.questionText: A tank is filled in 5 hours by three pipes A, B, and C. Pipe C is twice as fast as B and B is twice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Efficiencies: A = 1, B = 2, C = 4. Combined rate = 7 units/hr. Total capacity = 5 * 7 = 35 units. Time for A alone = 35 / 1 = 35 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 15 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together and after 3 minutes pipe A is closed, how much more time will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60. A = 5, B = 4. In 3 mins: 3 * 9 = 27 units. Remaining = 33 units. Time for B = 33 / 4 = 8.25 minutes (8 mins 15 secs).

questions.questionText: A pipe can empty a cistern in 15 hours and another pipe can empty it in 10 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the full cistern be emptied?
questions.explanation: Emptying rate = 1/15 + 1/10 = 5/30 = 1/6. Time = 6 hours.

questions.questionText: A cistern has three pipes A, B, and C. A and B can fill it in 4 and 5 hours respectively and C can empty it in 2 hours. If the pipes are opened in order at 1 pm, 2 pm, and 3 pm, when will the cistern be empty?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 20. A = +5, B = +4, C = -10. By 3 pm: A (2 hrs) = 10, B (1 hr) = 4. Total water at 3 pm = 14 units. At 3 pm, net rate = 5 + 4 - 10 = -1 unit/hr. Time to empty 14 units = 14 hours; if rates scaled to empty in 2 hours -> 5:00 pm.

questions.questionText: A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: Time for first half (1 tap) = 3 hours. For remaining half, 4 taps operate: time = 3 / 4 hour = 45 minutes. Total time = 3 hours 45 minutes.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. A third pipe C can empty it in 40 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?

A cistern is provided with two pipes A and B. Pipe A can fill it in 20 minutes and pipe B in 30 minutes. If both pipes are kept open for 10 minutes and then B is closed, in how much time will the cistern be full from the start?
questions.explanation: In 10 minutes, A and B fill 10 * (1/20 + 1/30) = 10 * (5/60) = 5/6 of the tank. Remaining = 1/6. Time for A = (1/6) / (1/20) = 20/6 = 3 1/3 mins. Total time from start = 10 + 3 1/3 = 13 1/3 minutes.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 minutes and 25 minutes respectively. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
A pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another can empty it in y hours (where y > x). If both are opened, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/x - 1/y = (y - x)/xy. Time taken = xy / (y - x) hours.

questions.questionText: Three taps A, B, and C fill a tank in 10, 15, and 30 hours respectively. If tap A is opened all the time, tap B for 2 hours, and tap C for 3 hours, what fraction of the tank is filled?
questions.explanation: Tap A runs for 3 hours and contributes 3/10 of the tank. Tap B contributes 2/15 and tap C contributes 3/30 = 1/10. The total is 3/10 + 2/15 + 1/10 = 8/15 of the tank.

questions.questionText: A cistern can be filled in 9 hours but due to a leak at the bottom, it takes 10 hours. If the cistern is full, in how many hours will it be emptied by the leak?
questions.explanation: 1/9 - 1/10 = 1/90. Leak empties full cistern in 90 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a water tank in 8 hours and 12 hours respectively. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, after how many hours should pipe B be closed so that the tank gets filled in 6 hours?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 24. A = 3, B = 2. A runs for 6 hours: 6 * 3 = 18 units. Remaining for B = 24 - 18 = 6 units. Time for B = 6 / 2 = 3 hours.

questions.questionText: A tank is filled by three pipes with uniform flow rates. The first two pipes operating together fill the tank in 4 hours. The second pipe fills the tank 6 hours faster than the third pipe. If the first pipe fills the tank in 6 hours, how long does the third pipe take?
questions.explanation: 1/A + 1/B = 1/4 => 1/6 + 1/B = 1/4 => 1/B = 1/4 - 1/6 = 1/12 => B takes 12 hours. Since B is 6 hours faster than C, C takes 12 + 6 = 18 hours.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours respectively. If both pipes are opened together, how much time will they take to fill 75% of the tank?

A pipe can fill a reservoir in 15 minutes and another can fill it in 20 minutes. A waste pipe can empty it in 30 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many minutes will the reservoir be filled?
Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. If both are opened together, after what time should A be closed so that the cistern is completely filled in 18 minutes?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 60 units. A = 3, B = 2. B runs for 18 mins: 18 * 2 = 36 units. Remaining for A = 60 - 36 = 24 units. Time for A = 24 / 3 = 8 minutes.
